finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl lets an unauthenticated client read arbitrary files readable by the server process.
finding.source: Query parameter f, read unvalidated at files.go:12
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13; contents written at files.go:18

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") takes attacker-controlled input with no validation
filepath.Join(root, name) calls Clean, which resolves .. segments, so the result is not confined to root=/srv/files
os.ReadFile reads the resolved path; errors return 404
Successful read is written to the response in full

finding.guards_checked: filepath.Join (cleans but does not confine); no .. rejection; no filepath.Rel or prefix check against root; no symlink check; no auth middleware; no content-type or allowlist. None block /dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 reads f with no validation; files.go:13 uses filepath.Join(root, name), which cleans the path, so ../ segments escape /srv/files; there is no ".." rejection, prefix/Rel containment check, or symlink check. The /dl route is registered without auth middleware at files.go:32, and download() has no authorization check before the read at files.go:13 or the write at files.go:18. The only check, the err test at files.go:14, only handles read failure and does not confine the path.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can send GET /dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd, which files.go:13 resolves outside root via filepath.Join's Clean, and files.go:18 returns the contents, with no effective control in between. The result depends on the process's file permissions, and deployment-level auth or a proxy is not visible in the provided code.

finding.claim: /dl and /avatar have no authentication or authorization, so any network client can fetch any file under /srv/files.
finding.source: Any network client reaching port 8082; handlers registered at files.go:32-33
finding.sink: Handlers download (files.go:11) and avatar (files.go:21) serve file contents

trace.note: http.HandleFunc registers /dl on the default mux with no wrapper
download performs no session, token, or ownership check
avatar performs no session, token, or ownership check

finding.guards_checked: No middleware, no handler-level auth, no ownership check. Precondition: an authenticating reverse proxy in front of the service would reduce risk, but nothing in this repo enforces one.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:32-33 register /dl and /avatar directly on the default mux with no wrapper, and download (files.go:11-19) and avatar (files.go:21-29) read and return file contents with no session, token, or ownership check. The only mitigation the candidate mentions, an authenticating reverse proxy, is not in this repo (the only other files are .claude/skills/security-research/* docs and files.go), so it cannot be verified here.
verdict.reason: Anonymous network clients can reach /dl and /avatar on :8082 (files.go:32-34), and the handlers serve file contents without any auth check (files.go:11-29), so the candidate's trace is accurate and no in-repo control blocks it; a deployment-level proxy or firewall could still reduce exposure, but that is outside the code I could inspect.

finding.claim: Unbounded os.ReadFile on special or large files allows memory exhaustion and goroutine hangs (DoS).
finding.source: Query parameter f via traversal (see F1), or any large or FIFO file under root
finding.sink: os.ReadFile at files.go:13 (and files.go:23 in avatar)

trace.note: Join resolves to a special file such as /dev/zero, or to a FIFO or very large file
os.ReadFile reads to EOF and allocates all of it in memory; /dev/zero never reaches EOF, and a FIFO blocks the goroutine
ListenAndServe uses default server settings with no timeouts or size limits

finding.guards_checked: No Stat for regular-file or size checks; no io.LimitReader; no server timeouts. Not verified by execution.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:13 has no os.Stat or size check and no io.LimitReader, and files.go:23 has none either. files.go:34 uses http.ListenAndServe with default settings. Only the error branch at files.go:14-16 exists, and it does not bound the read.
verdict.reason: The download handler at files.go:12-13 passes an unauthenticated query value through filepath.Join(root, name) into os.ReadFile with no size or type check, so a request that resolves to /dev/zero (via the traversal in F1) or to a very large file under /srv/files forces unbounded allocation at files.go:13. The FIFO case blocks only that request's goroutine, not the whole server, so the "goroutine hangs" part of the claim is overstated, but the memory-exhaustion DoS holds.

finding.claim: The plaintext HTTP service is bound to all interfaces with no TLS, exposing file contents in transit.
finding.sink: http.ListenAndServe serving file contents over cleartext on 0.0.0.0 and [::]

trace.note: No TLS configuration; handlers return raw file bytes over HTTP

finding.guards_checked: No TLS, no bind-address restriction, no ReadHeaderTimeout. Severity depends on network exposure, which the repo does not show.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:34 calls http.ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) with no TLS config, and there is no reverse proxy, bind-address restriction, or TLS wrapper in the repo. The handlers at files.go:18 and files.go:28 write raw file bytes to the response.
verdict.reason: At files.go:34 the server listens in cleartext on all interfaces, and files.go:18 and files.go:28 return raw file contents, so any network observer on a path to the host can read the data in transit; severity depends on the deployment's network exposure, which the repo does not show.
